free_tier.stated: The space given to you on this server is given for the expressed purpose of advancing free software that can run in free operating systems, documenting such software, or creating free educational textbooks.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The Download Area page states no per-file size limit; uploads are made with scp or rsync into /releases/GROUP_NAME/.

retention.stated: Our intent is to provide a permanent home for all versions of your project. We do reserve the right, however, to discontinue hosting a project.
retention.notes: In order to preserve history and complete transparency, projects that contain anything substantive are not removed.

egress.terms: Files at download.savannah.nongnu.org/releases/GROUP_NAME/ are multiplexed between all mirrors, and an upload can take up to 24 hours to appear on all mirrors. unverified: no egress charge or volume quota is stated on the page.

tooling: SSH public-key auth only. Upload via scp (the -O flag is mandatory, see limits) or rsync to download.savannah.nongnu.org releases directory. Removal via restricted SSH commands ssh host rm or rmdir. Gnulib build-aux gnupload script is supported. Read side is plain anonymous HTTP from the mirror ring.
chaining: Each non-GNU package submitted for hosting is evaluated and approved by Savannah administrators. Limits on files, versions or groups: unverified, not stated on the pages read.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published. Structural caps that matter more: (1) SFTP IS DISABLED - announced 2023-11, 'we've found a vulnerability in our SFTP setup, and couldn't fix it otherwise than completely disabling SFTP. This affects uploading files to the *download* host'. Because OpenSSH >= 9.0 makes scp use SFTP by default, `scp -O` is required or every upload fails. (2) GPG-signing is expected (the docs tell you to upload foo.tar.gz + foo.tar.gz.sig) though not enforced: 'unlike ftp.gnu.org, Savannah doesn't enforce using GPG signatures for releases'. (3) Write access requires a registered SSH key on the account.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Two real breakages. First, SFTP-off is a live trap for any modern client - a naive `scp` on OpenSSH 9+ silently fails. Second, the mirror ring is uneven: the same lzip tarball (123,850 bytes) took 4.6 s once and timed out at 21 s on the redirect target (ftp.cc.uoc.gr) another time, so per-mirror health varies and single-stream fetch is not trustworthy. Site pages also intermittently serve a Kant-quoting anti-scraper page instead of content - the register/ and requirements.php URLs both did this via the reader while the Wayback copy of the same page was clean.

extras.quota_verbatim: No published byte quota found on any Savannah page - the hosting-requirements doc speaks only in terms of purpose ('The space given to you on this server is given for the expressed purpose of advancing free software') and permanence ('Our intent is to provide a permanent home for all versions of your project'), never a number. Disk was moved to Ceph/NFS precisely to remove the old ceiling (savannah-hackers-public, 2019-04: 'This increases the disk space and moves onto the new cephs storage').
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: none published. Structural caps that matter more: (1) SFTP IS DISABLED - announced 2023-11, 'we've found a vulnerability in our SFTP setup, and couldn't fix it otherwise than completely disabling SFTP. This affects uploading files to the *download* host'. Because OpenSSH >= 9.0 makes scp use SFTP by default, `scp -O` is required or every upload fails. (2) GPG-signing is expected (the docs tell you to upload foo.tar.gz + foo.tar.gz.sig) though not enforced: 'unlike ftp.gnu.org, Savannah doesn't enforce using GPG signatures for releases'. (3) Write access requires a registered SSH key on the account.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free and mirrored: `download.savannah.{gnu,nongnu}.org` redirect to a world-wide mirror ring. Verified live: a GET 302s to a national mirror (fosszone.csd.auth.gr) which serves 200 with real bytes. No metering, no billing.
extras.chaining_verbatim: One Savannah group per project, unlimited files per group, unlimited versions retained forever. Accounts are free; the gate is that a human evaluates the package ('Evaluate and approve non-gnu packages submitted for hosting'), so cardinality is bounded by reviewer throughput, not by quota. For GNU packages ftp.gnu.org/alpha.gnu.org is a second surface with an automated signed-upload path.
extras.tooling_verbatim: SSH public-key auth only. Upload with `scp -O <file> <file>.sig LOGIN@download.savannah.nongnu.org:/releases/GROUP_NAME/` (the `-O` is mandatory - see limits) or `rsync -tv`. Removal via restricted SSH commands `ssh host rm <path>` / `rmdir`. Also the `gnupload` script from Gnulib's build-aux. Read side is plain anonymous HTTP from the mirror ring.
extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture this session.
